summary: The Pulse room admits its contact on the room grant alone (Amine 26/10, S24 3289), and the WhatsApp allowlist owner sends direct-rule changes as an RFC 7396 merge patch so lowering a scope or removing a contact really removes its prompt.
reason: S24 26/10 14:25:59Z, operation sadok-scope-standard-20261026 (Amine: remove Sadok's Zain Bahrain custom scope): the owner sent the whole channels.whatsapp.direct map under replacePaths, but the Gateway's config.patch (OpenClaw 2026.9.6 applyMergePatch) merges objects and replacePaths only replaces arrays. The Gateway logged « config.patch noop (no changed paths) », verification failed, the receipt was indeterminate and the contact kept its custom prompt and metadata (effect verified absent). Any scope lowering, suspension or removal that drops a direct rule had the same defect; the test Gateway replaced the map wholesale and hid it. Separately, _native_pulse_context_read refused any Pulse room contact with a custom conversation scope, a scope prompt or a compacted contactMemory (Sadok on 26/10 14:16Z: NATIVE_ROOM_ACCESS_UNVERIFIED, reply « L’accès actuel à la pièce Pulse n’est pas établi »). Amine decided that whoever has the Pulse room can do everything in Pulse through it, without global owner privileges; the conversation scope and memory only shape the model agent, which the native path never runs.
